title: Female borrowers who mention the educational needs of their children may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific loan amounts or the lending organization may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who address lenders directly in their pitch may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention specific towns or regions in their pitch may fund faster.
Male borrowers who mention education or learning conditions for themselves or their children may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention using the loan for basic survival needs, such as food, may fund more slowly.
Pitches from women that explicitly mention securing the future of their family are associated with increased funding speed.
Pitches from women that specify the number, age, or schooling status of their children are associated with increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who include their age in the pitch may fund faster.
Detailed descriptions of local geography may slow funding for male borrowers.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Emphasizing professional goals, business quality, or reputation predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Emphasizing family roles or family-related financial struggles predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
